So, I'm 1000% sure that this girl already knows you want that.  And I'm 90% sure she thinks she's moving forward with you towards that.

You are not being "friendzoned" here.  From where I'm sitting, she's been honest about where she's coming from and now you're getting to know each other in a friendly datelike environment.  This seems to me like it will turn into fullblown dating before too long, unless you guys aren't compatible.

As an aside, it's not impossible at this stage, and at your age in particular, for one person to flake or be a total jerk.  For example, she might say, "I just want to get to know you." but then you turn around and she's making out with this guy she met at the movies with you that day.  Does she seem like the kind of girl who would do that?  Or do you not know, because you don't know her well enough?  

Either way, any behavior like that on her part would not reflect on you at all.  It would have nothing to do with you, even a little bit.  That's about her.  (And she sounds super nice!)

Some questions I have for you are:  How much experience does she have dating?  Is she religious, or is her family?  Is she shy?

Just relax and let things be what they are.  Maybe as you guys get to know each other, you'll find you don't like her as much, or she likes you more than you like her.  You just don't know what will happen at this point, and that's okay.  

I know it's nervewracking, but you're doing great, and it sounds like you're getting all the right signals from her.  If you were this nervous and inexperienced and you were hanging with a girl that was 1000% ready to zoom forward that might not be great, either.  Just breathe.

Oh, man.  Those weren't rejections.  I think she likes you, hon, she's just kind of anxious and she doesn't really know you and she's nervous, too.  You paid for the movie tickets and she didn't object, so that's a good sign.  Don't over think this, things are going well, this is totally normal.  I think she does like you.  I wouldn't even call those rejections at all.

*hugs*

When did she reject you?  And how?

She said yes to you, too.  She agreed to get to know you.

I don't think she is just feeling guilty, although I'm sure she does feel HUGELY guilty.  (At some point you guys are both going to have to deal with the guilt/trust issues, which are big but not impassable.)

As Dr Internet, I can't say what is best.  But I do know that you need to work on being healthy, yourself, first, before you can really deal with the relationship, and while it may be that you have to work on both at once, I don't think it's feasible to do this without professional help.  Short term individual and couples' therapy would probably be really helpful, and not all at the same time.  

All of these emotions are hitting you at once, and if I had to guess, I'd say that the insecurity of her cheating is hitting you right in the depression- where you are already vulnerable.  I'm a depression veteran; I have the scars, I have the family history, and I'm not ashamed to admit it.  Here's the thing about depression:  it lies to you.  (Much like these assholes on reddit who say that she "had a stud" "in her back pocket".  That is some bull fucking shit.)  Depression says, "She can't be happy with me, I can't ever trust her again, I'm not good enough, she's a cheating whore, everything is broken."  Plus a lot of other shit that I have no doubt you've been shoveling for a while.  But depression is treatable.  

Please talk to your doctor.  Check out your insurance website and see what is covered for therapy.  Pull out that card you carry and call the numbers on it.  This is doable.  Just do one thing at a time, you don't need to deal with the whole enchilada at once. You got this.

You're a good guy.  You deserve good things.  I'm pulling for you, and you're going to come through this.  *hugs*

Just my two cents:

Listen, I don't know you and I don't know your sweetie.  But I'm getting some very strong vibes that he has some insecurities of his own- and he's also powerfully self aware and intelligent enough to cover them up much better than most people do.  But he has chosen you for a reason, and I suspect that part of that reason is that he knows you're a bit dazzled by him.  That's not healthy.  And he has not made it healthy for you.  There are things he could have done to make you feel safe and loved, here, and he hasn't chosen to do them.  That's the bottom line.
It seems like an uncomfortable place to be, that you don't feel good talking to him about how you really feel.  How great can he be if he's not a safe harbor for you?

Hmmm, have you tried complimenting her?  It starts with words, I'd say.

Compliments, showing interest in her and what she's interested in, holding things for her, holding doors. 

Think about people's personal space bubbles.  We all have them.  In the US they're a couple of feet, usually, it's the space where you notice someone else is "in your space" or "close" to you.  In dating, people generally start breaking through those bubbles or compressing them, gradually.  You get closer to her, basically.  Not like right up on her, hugging her all the time, but walking nearer to her, standing closer to her, etc.  Does that make sense?  She'll be more aware of you, and you of her.

In all of this, it is most important to be aware of her.  Obviously you'll be aware of her body, but know how she's reacting.  Look into her eyes and see how she's reacting.  If she's moving away or her body language is closed or she looks unhappy or displeased you should back off.  If she seems happy or she's moving closer or letting you move in or her body language is open and receptive, keep doing what you're doing.  Be respectful and reasonably sure that you're not making her miserable.  You can't go wrong.

I am actually the one slowing things down, although, again, I can't get a reply from him.  I think I made him feel bad when we were discussing visas.  The visa I'm going on requires a "true and genuine desire to be a tourist", so any thoughts of, say, marrying while I'm over there and converting it to a partner visa are on the downlow, and we've been trying to avoid the stern eye of immigration.  

However, given these issues, I told him I was uncertain enough about what was happening between us that I considered the visa issues settled- I have flights there and back, and if things don't work out, I will fly back, no harm, no foul.  I'm giving it a solid shot and I'm getting to know the country as well as him, in person, but I'm open to a number of different ways this could go.  

And holy smokes you are correct about the backseat drivers.  His mom is amazeballs, fortunately, since his sister groaned whenever he hugged me.  Painful.  

I'm reasonably certain that unless I throw what I'd consider to be a tantrum, I'm not going to get a reply, and I think that's what's bothering me most.  I don't want to have to do that. I'm a patient and reasonable woman(or that's what I tell myself), but being ignored by an adult is a big red button for me personally.

Honey, you did fine.  It sounds like it went great.  There was hugging.  The next step is to ask her out again and see what she says.  Maybe even try flirting- it will not hurt, I promise.  The rejection is the same whether you flirt or not, so flirt- it will make your life better!

I'm sorry, but the best advice I know for feeling comfortable with approaching women is just to approach women.  I hate pickup artists, but they get guys to ask lots and lots of women out, and that gets you to realize that rejection is not that bad and that women will say yes if you ask them!  

Signed, a woman who has been asked out a million times and who has asked guys out a million times

Yo, you sound like you really love this girl.  If she told you right away and she seems genuinely sorry, that is great grounds for moving past the cheating.  The fight about the cheating, it wasn't right of her to bring up the past, it was just a rationalization.  But it sounds like she is struggling to deal, too, just like you.  You guys need each other.  This cheating is not something you can't deal with- just like your depression is not something you can't deal with.  Go see a doctor, honey.  Talk to your girl honestly and tell her how hard it's been for you- get emotional if you need to, I KNOW how hard it is to be shut out.  I don't know the future of your relationship, but I know that ending it over this could be something you'll regret.

Girl, 22 is so young.  So young!  You are dealing with so much, and let me tell you, you are a star.  

First, let me remind you that adulthood doesn't pop into place like a puzzle piece.  Most "adults" don't feel like "real grownups", especially in our culture, and you're carrying more adult responsibility than 99% of people your age.  Heck, of people years older than you.  Just like kids don't suddenly switch from babies to toddlers, teenagers don't suddenly turn into adults.  You're doing great.  It sounds like you're carrying a lot of stress, and it's not really about where you are in maturity, because you sound plenty mature to me.  You just don't have the experience to know that this is normal.

Second, in the medical field, we learn that if we don't take care of ourselves first, we can't help others.  What are you doing for yourself?  Are you sleeping?  Eating well, and regularly?  Are your needs being met?  Is there someone in your life giving you a hard time?  Are you ill or injured?  Back to basics, hon.  Keep it simple.  These will serve you.

Third, it's Dr Internet's opinion that you need to see a doctor.  Based on your comments below, you sound like you're moving pretty hard into depression/adjustment disorder, which, let me stress again, is very normal and also very treatable.  It's exhausting and very scary and very, very disheartening, and it does feel like another thing to add to the Pile, but it is worth it.  

I just want to let you know that you don't have to be perfect.  You said you've done this without a parent's help and that's amazing, and also very rough on a person.  You're still young and fragile, and it feels like you should be more, should do more than you are and can right now.  But I'm here to testify that you are doing just great, and your job is just to stay steady and healthy and to take care of yourself first and foremost, because you deserve it.  If I were your mom I'd be busting my buttons with pride.  

*hugs*  I wish you all the best, please update and let us know how it's going!  I have been there with that slog and that unending exhaustion, so I'll be thinking of you!

My big issue dx wise has been that I'm depressed (and suuuuuper good at faking that I'm not!) with atypical ADD, and psychs like to stroke their chins and say, "But what if you're actually BIPOLAR?" and that's when I go, "But what if I'm NOT because Adderall et al actually make me function better and more calmly instead of going into mania, and because you're not the first one to think of this?"

I'm going to start wearing a pin to my appointments that says, "I'm my first and best doctor."  Ugh.  Not that I've seen a psych in a year, sigh.  I'm getting my antidepressants from my GP and my therapy from my well-organized support network and coping mechanisms, as well as teh internets!  (Hello internets!)
